arb-tax-decay.title: The longer it sits, the more the next swap pays
arb-tax-decay.lede: This pool prices staleness. Trade it twice in a row and the second swap is cheap; leave it alone and the price of going first climbs.
arb-tax-decay.liveLabel: the fee right now, given how long the pool has been quiet
arb-tax-decay.compareHint: Swap twice in quick succession: the second one is cheaper, because the pool was not stale.

priority-fee-tax.title: What you bid for position is what you pay
priority-fee-tax.lede: Racing flow bids for its place in the block. This pool reads that bid and charges for it.
priority-fee-tax.liveLabel: the fee for a swap at the current priority fee

curve.name: feeAtPriority
curve.xLabel: priority fee bid, gwei per gas

markout-fee.title: A fee that learns what its own flow is worth
markout-fee.lede: The pool grades each swap after the fact by whether the price kept moving its way, and prices the next one from the running average.
markout-fee.liveLabel: the fee at the toxicity this pool has measured

anti-snipe-ramp.title: Sniping the first block buys nothing
anti-snipe-ramp.lede: The pool opens at a punitive fee that decays to normal, and every cent of the difference goes to liquidity providers rather than the deployer.
anti-snipe-ramp.liveLabel: the fee at this point in the ramp

trading-calendar.title: A session, priced rather than enforced
trading-calendar.lede: The pool never stops quoting. Outside its trading session immediacy simply costs more, and the open and close are ramps rather than cliffs.
trading-calendar.liveLabel: the fee at this moment in the week

localDeploy.config: TradingCalendarHook.Config({openSecond: 13 hours + 30 minutes, closeSecond: 20 hours, rampSeconds: 30 minutes, sessionFee: 500, closedFee: 20_000, daysMask: 0x1F})

expiry-settle.title: Moving the settlement price gets dearer as it approaches
expiry-settle.lede: The fee ramps quadratically into maturity, so the print is most expensive to move exactly when moving it would pay most.
expiry-settle.liveLabel: the fee at this distance from maturity

step-curve.title: A quote that holds still
step-curve.lede: This pool prices in increments. Inside a band the quote is firm and a swap has no slippage at all; crossing one steps the price.

localDeploy.constructorArgs: IPoolManager(address(manager)), 2 * Q96, Q96 / 100, Q96 / 2, 1e18, 30, "Step Curve LP", "STEP-LP"

power-perp.title: Pick your exposure
power-perp.lede: A weighted geometric mean, so a provider chooses how much of the price move they want instead of always getting the square root of it.

yield-space.title: A pool that quotes a yield
yield-space.lede: The curve knows about the calendar: it converges to par at maturity on its own, so nobody has to be paid to arbitrage it there.

grid-ladder.title: A pool that quotes a bid and an ask
grid-ladder.lede: Two independent ladders, so the pool holds a market maker's position rather than a fee schedule. Buying always costs more than selling fetches.

epoch-rebalance.title: An index whose future is fixed before you deposit
epoch-rebalance.lede: The weight schedule is set at deployment and glides continuously, so the allocation on any future date is computable and no single block is worth racing to.

circuit-breaker.title: A pool that stops rather than being drained
circuit-breaker.lede: After a move larger than its threshold the pool halts swaps for a cooldown and resumes on its own. Withdrawals are never blocked.

oracle-band.title: A pool that will not be walked away from reality
oracle-band.lede: Swaps must clear inside a band around a signed reference price. Outside it the pool declines, and says by how much.

drawdown-cap.title: A cap on how far one address can move the price
drawdown-cap.lede: Each address gets a price-impact budget per epoch. Spend it and the pool declines the rest until the epoch turns.

reads.label: Ticks of impact left this epoch

depeg-shield.title: Fees that fight the depeg
depeg-shield.lede: The further the pool drifts from its peg, the more a swap that widens the gap pays, and the less one that closes it does.

reads.label: Fee to push away from the peg
Fee to push back toward it

dutch-clearing-launch.title: The pool will not sell below its schedule
dutch-clearing-launch.lede: A descending floor. Buy below it and the pool refuses; wait and the floor comes to you. Selling is never restricted.

localDeploy.config: DutchClearingLaunchHook.Config({startPriceX96: uint160(4 * Q96), floorPriceX96: uint160(Q96 / 2), startTime: uint64(block.timestamp), duration: 3600, buyIsZeroForOne: false})
